title: Hip Abduction Machine
summary: Seated machine: push the knees apart against the pads. Hip abductors 1 (glute medius and minimus, plus TFL), glutes 0.3.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: The glute medius, glute minimus and TFL move the thigh out to the side (hip abduction), the motion this machine loads.
The upper glute max helps abduct, more if you lean forward; minor (0.3).

setup.text: Sit with the pads on the outside of your knees.
Set the start width so the pads are touching with a little tension.

form_cues.cue: Push the knees out against the pads
form_cues.why: Pushing with the knees, not the feet, keeps the hips doing the work.
A brief pause at the widest point stops the stack from swinging.
Controlling the return keeps tension on.

form_cues.cue: Leaning forward slightly works the glute medius more.
form_cues.why: Leaning forward bends the hip, shifting more work to the glute max.

form_cues.cue: Keep your back on the pad
form_cues.why: A stable torso makes the reps comparable.

bias_tweaks.change: Lean forward from the hips (torso about 45 degrees)
bias_tweaks.effect: With the hip bent, the upper glute max helps more.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Rocking the torso to push the pads out.
mistakes.fix: Use a load you can move with steady control.
Use the full range of the machine.

mistakes.text: Letting the stack slam between reps.

misconceptions.myth: The abduction machine burns hip fat.
misconceptions.reality: Training a muscle doesn't selectively reduce the fat over it.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Low-risk to push close to failure.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Standing, one leg at a time with a cuff.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Lying on your side; no equipment.

notes: Abductor exercises have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
